Photosynthesis

Photosynthesis is the way green plants make their own food from light. Plants take in water through their roots and carbon dioxide from the air. Inside the leaves, a green pigment called chlorophyll captures light energy from the sun. The plant uses that energy to turn water and carbon dioxide into glucose, a kind of sugar. Oxygen is released as a waste product, and animals breathe it in.

Light reactions

In the light reactions, chlorophyll absorbs light and splits water molecules. This makes energy carriers that the plant will use in the next stage. These steps happen in the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast, which are stacked like coins.

Calvin cycle

In the Calvin cycle, the plant uses those energy carriers to build glucose from carbon dioxide. This stage does not need light directly, so it is sometimes called the dark reactions, even though it happens during the day.
